rules.name: Disk or volume destruction
rules.reason: Formats or wipes a disk or volume (irreversible). Free space by deleting specific project files; leave disk operations to the user.

rules.name: Recursive or forced deletion
rules.reason: Recursive or forced delete. List the target first, then delete only the specific workspace files or directories the task needs.

rules.name: Bulk deletion by wildcard or mirror sync
rules.reason: Bulk wildcard delete, mirror or truncate can erase more than intended. Name the exact files, or list the matches first and delete them explicitly.

rules.name: Raw device or boot write
rules.reason: Writes to a raw device or boot configuration (can destroy the disk or stop the machine booting). Write to a regular file; leave device and boot changes to the user.

rules.name: Credential destruction or dump
rules.reason: Deletes or dumps credentials or keys. Leave ~/.ssh, cloud credentials and system secrets alone; tell the user if a credential change is needed.

rules.name: Privilege escalation or backdoor account
rules.reason: Gains root or creates privileged access. Run the command without sudo or elevation, or tell the user it needs administrator rights.

rules.name: System integrity tampering
rules.reason: Changes system configuration (hosts, sshd, SELinux, services) or force-kills processes. Use project-local configuration, or tell the user a system change is needed.

rules.name: Downloaded code, reverse shell, or trusted-tool execution
rules.reason: Downloads and runs remote code or opens a remote shell. Download to a file, inspect it, then run a known local command.

rules.name: Log clearing or clock changes
rules.reason: Clears system logs or changes the system clock. Leave both alone; write your own output to a project file.

rules.name: Persistence
rules.reason: Installs a scheduled task or service that outlives the session. Run the work now in the foreground, or tell the user it needs a scheduled job.

rules.name: Backup or shadow-copy deletion
rules.reason: Deletes backups, shadow copies or Docker volumes (unrecoverable). Remove only the specific containers or images you created and keep volumes.

rules.name: Database destruction
rules.reason: Drops or truncates a database or table. Use a scoped DELETE ... WHERE on a test database, or tell the user a destructive migration is needed.

rules.name: Destructive Git operation
rules.reason: Rewrites or discards git history (force push, reset --hard, clean -fdx, filter-branch). Commit or stash first, use git revert or a new branch, push without --force.

rules.name: Shutdown, restart, or logoff
rules.reason: Shuts down, reboots or logs off the machine. Stop only the processes you started.

rules.name: Dangerous chmod or chown
rules.reason: Makes files world-writable or re-owns system paths recursively. Grant only the permission the task needs on specific project files.

rules.name: Dynamic code evaluation
rules.reason: Runs code through eval, python -c or node -e, which hides what executes. Write the code to a file in the workspace and run that file.

rules.name: Data exfiltration or packaging
rules.reason: Packs, encrypts or syncs data to remote storage. Keep the data local; tell the user if an upload is really required.

rules.name: Kernel module or dangerous sysctl operation
rules.reason: Loads kernel modules, preloads libraries or changes kernel parameters. Leave the kernel alone; tell the user if the task needs it.

rules.name: Fork bomb
rules.reason: Fork bomb that exhausts the machine. Never run it.

rules.name: Recursive/forced delete (strict)
rules.reason: Any rm with -r or -f is blocked at the strict level. Delete specific files without -r/-f.

rules.name: Destructive git (strict)
rules.reason: Destructive git command blocked at the strict level. Use git revert, a new branch, or a dry run such as git clean -n.

rules.name: Root/system/home/credential delete
rules.reason: Deletes a root, system, home or credential directory. Delete only specific paths inside the workspace.

rules.name: macOS disk erase/partition
rules.reason: Erases or repartitions a disk with diskutil or newfs. Leave disk operations to the user.

rules.name: macOS system/home/volume delete
rules.reason: Deletes a macOS system directory, a user home or a whole volume. Delete only specific paths inside the workspace.

path_reasons.protected: Writes into a system or credential location. Write inside the workspace instead.
path_reasons.control: Writes to Omnigent's permission files for this session. Leave them alone; the user changes the permission tier from the session header.
